artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Hope Community Church complained that Central Carolina Presbytery erred in adopting a policy requiring a multi-site session to eventually particularize its second worship site as a distinct new church. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO expressly vests the Session with authority over the time and place of worship and the Presbytery's mandatory particularization requirement exceeded its constitutional powers and was annulled.

artifacts.title: Western Carolina v. Tennessee Valley
artifacts.synopsis: Western Carolina Presbytery and two other presbyteries requested the General Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over a teaching elder regarding allegations that women preachers filled the pulpit at Cedar Springs Presbyterian Church. The Standing Judicial Commission dismissed the matter as not properly before the General Assembly, ruling that the conduct of worship services is under the jurisdiction of the Session, not subject to process against a minister under BCO 34-1, and that Tennessee Valley Presbytery did act on the allegations.
